messages:
Nadia (Acct): Hi team — we ran into a blocking issue. Our app hit the monthly token limit right at 23:50 UTC on the last day and started getting 429s. We expected a reset at midnight UTC but tokens stayed at 0 until our console showed a reset at 00:07. Can you explain the 7-minute delay? We had a scheduled job at 00:05 and it failed.

Asha (Support): sorry about that, thanks for the report! quick Qs: which org id and which plan? did you top up or purchase more credits before midnight? any billing emails?

Nadia (Acct): Org: redwood-acct-981. We're on the standard monthly plan (metred tokens). No manual top-up. We only rely on the monthly allotment. We saw the 429s with response headers: `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Quota-Reset: 1700000000` (not sure what that value is), and then after 00:07 we saw `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 500000`.

Asha (Support): thanks — that header `X-Quota-Reset` is unix epoch for reset time. looking at our side, the canonical reset time for monthly quotas is aligned to 00:00 UTC of the first day of the new cycle, but there can be a short processing window where billing/usage aggregation finalizes. usually under a minute but sometimes up to ~10 minutes during high-load windows (end-of-month churn).

Tom (Billing): adding context from billing: when monthly quotas flip we run two steps: 1) usage aggregation job that consolidates per-tenant usage into the billing DB, and 2) quota provisioning which writes the new token balance to the serving config. If either step is delayed (DB lag, heavy job queue) the serving layer continues to enforce the previous balance until it reads the new balance. That explains the ~7m you observed. We try to make that <60s but end-of-month spikes can push it out.

Nadia (Acct): ok, that helps. Is the `X-Quota-Reset` header supposed to show the new reset epoch or the scheduled reset? The header we got looked like an older epoch.

Kai (SRE): the header should reflect the reset epoch we expect the provisioner to apply next. however some older edge servers cache quota meta for 300s TTL. during a flip we invalidate cache but if invalidation messages are delayed the header may be stale for a short while. headers you pasted look like a pre-flip value. We push invalidations over the message bus and fallback to periodic refresh every 5 minutes, so worst-case you might see a few mins of mismatch.

Asha (Support): tl;dr: reset happens at 00:00 UTC, but you can see a small window where the serving layer hasn't picked up the newly provisioned credits due to aggregation + cache invalidation latency. This is expected behavior in extreme end-of-month load but rare.

Nadia (Acct): is there an SLA for that? our job is time-sensitive — we need to avoid failures in that 10-minute window. Any mitigation?

Kai (SRE): mitigation options: 1) enable short burst buffer (if available) — this keeps a small reserve for last-minute spikes, 2) use a soft-fail fallback to a cheaper model if 429s occur (tooling suggestion below), 3) schedule critical jobs away from midnight UTC, or 4) we can enable a temporary guardrail for your org to prioritize quota provisioning (needs billing approval).

Asha (Support): also note: if you have auto-topup/chargeable overage enabled, purchases processed before the aggregation job completes will still be reflected after the same provisioning delay (i.e., there's no magic immediate credit until the billing job commits). If you need instant capacity at month boundary, auto-topup still subjects you to that ~processing latency unless you pre-buy credits and we pre-provision them into the serving config earlier in the day.

Nadia (Acct): what about prorated purchases — if we buy extra credits at 23:58 UTC will we get them before midnight?

Tom (Billing): purchases go through payment processing then into accounting queue. If the charge clears immediately and the accounting job picks it up, it's possible to see the new balance before midnight but not guaranteed. For guaranteed availability for that minute we recommend buying credits earlier in the day or contacting support ahead of the cutoff so we can perform a manual pre-provision.

Nadia (Acct): got it. Can you put this in writing for my ops team? Also can you review our logs and confirm the exact window we were blocked so we can open a postmortem internally.

Asha (Support): yes. attaching a short summary and we will run a focused check of your org's provisioning events around the flip.

quota-bot: automated note: Creating support ticket #SUP-20260315-887 for org redwood-acct-981. Assigned to Asha (Support). Priority: P2.

Kai (SRE): for the ops team — quick repro and mitigations you can copy: 
1) Detect 429 with these headers: `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-Quota-Reset` (epoch).
2) On 429 -> immediate retry with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts, then fallback to alternate model/route. Example pseudo: 
```
if (resp.status == 429) {
  await sleep(expBackoff(attempt));
  retry();
  // if still 429 after 3 tries -> call fallbackModel()
}
```
3) Add instrumentation to log `quota.headers` and `quota.provision_event` and correlate to `billing.charges` for the minute around 00:00 UTC.

Kai (SRE): sample curl to inspect headers: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Look for `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-Quota-Reset` in the response.

Asha (Support): action items for us: 1) we will run the provisioner trace for your org around 1769120000-1769127200 to show when the aggregation job committed and when serving picked it up. 2) Billing will check for any processed charges near that minute. 3) I'll escalate to infra to investigate if cache invalidations were unusually delayed. We'll post findings in this thread.

Tom (Billing): FYI — I can enable a one-time manual pre-provision for your next month if you want guaranteed no-gap at flip. that requires a short billing approval and we can do it before your renewal.

Nadia (Acct): that would be great. please enable that for the next flip and share doc with the ops team. thank you — appreciate the quick responses. :pray:

Asha (Support): noted — I created a follow-up with billing and infra. leaving this thread open until we post the trace. :thumbsup:
